meta.tagline: Official reports, rain, and which forecast held
meta.description: Public board that sets weather forecasts beside measured rain and river level, and keeps a tally of which calls held. The August 2026 Galchhi–Rasuwagadhi fiber board stays on the same site.
meta.notOfficial: Not a warning from NDRRMA or the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology. Not affiliated with NDRRMA, DHM, NTC, Ncell, NTA, or China Telecom

home.title: What the ground shows, and which forecast held
home.lead: Weather forecasts beside the rain and river level the Department has measured. A trailing 24-hour gauge is not a model’s calendar day. The address of this site is unchanged.
home.checkBody: Taal in Manang has 125.6 mm in the last 24 hours. Chandrapur in Rautahat, nearest to the Bagmati Terai model point, has 28.8 mm. Bagmati at Khokana is on its warning line. Saturday’s model totals are not scored yet.
home.fiberNote: The Rasuwa Bhote Koshi flood and the Galchhi–Rasuwagadhi fiber cut. A different incident from Cyclone Arnab. Both stay on this site.
home.districtsNote: Roll-up from NTC public statements. “Remaining” means not yet back in service at that time.
home.routingCtaNote: Observed from RIPE RIS and linked to Hurricane Electric. China-side paths can be under-counted.
home.howToReadBody: The check page compares weather forecasts with measured rain and river level. It does not keep a casualty count. Green/amber/red chips below are the August fiber incident, curated from public NTC and news reports, with an as-of time. The routing page is a separate, live observation of BGP — not a substitute for those field reports, and not a repaired fiber.
home.starlinkNote: Starlink is not a licensed public restoration path in Nepal. Notes below record policy status and rumoured use only.
home.floodCta: Cyclone Arnab: which rivers can leave their gorge in minutes, and where Friday–Saturday rain is actually showing up.
home.cropsTitle: Crops, lakes, and a satellite check
home.cropsBody: Cited glacial-lake counts, crop losses named in news, and a box you draw. A rain gauge is not a loss. The free view opens first. A buy button leaves this site for the company’s page.

corridor.title: Corridor and sites
corridor.lead: The Kathmandu–China terrestrial path via Galchhi, Trishuli, Syabrubesi and Rasuwagadhi, plus the secondary Tatopani–Khasa crossing. Microwave radio is the documented backup north of Trishuli while fiber is cut.
corridor.mapHint: OpenStreetMap. Pins only for places with known coordinates — unnamed reports stay in the list.

satellites.title: Satellites over the flood corridor
satellites.lead: Public NASA daily true-color of the Galchhi–Rasuwagadhi valley from the day before the flood, plus live positions of Earth-observing satellites. This is geography and spacecraft, not people.
satellites.caveat: VIIRS true-color is hundreds of metres per pixel and the monsoon is often cloudy — you will not see a fiber cut. We do not locate phones, vehicles, or people. Starlink overhead is not a licensed internet service in Nepal.
satellites.imageryTitle: Daily NASA true-color / cloud view (GIBS / VIIRS)
satellites.imageryHint: Date starts at 25 August 2026 (day before the flood). Cloud is weather, not “no data.” The blue line is an approximate Bhotekoshi–Trishuli valley centerline (north → south), not a surveyed river GIS layer.
satellites.liveTitle: Spacecraft with a view of the valley
satellites.liveHint: A satellite counts if the valley is above 8° elevation from its antenna — not whether its ground track sits inside the little map box. GEO weather sats sit over the equator; they still see Rasuwa. Click a card to open that craft’s free public viewer (video or latest imagery), when one exists.
satellites.error: Live catalog unavailable. Imagery still works. Try Worldview below.
satellites.noneNear: None of the tracked spacecraft currently see the valley above 8° elevation.
satellites.s1Hint: C-band SAR from ASF, native frame (not stretched onto the map — that squeeze was a georeferencing artefact). Sees through cloud. Step the dates to track the valley. Click the large still for a full-size view.
satellites.credit: Optical: NASA EOSDIS GIBS. Radar stills: ASF DAAC / Copernicus Sentinel-1. Orbits: SatNOGS TLEs and published GEO slots. Map: OpenStreetMap.

routing.title: How traffic is being routed
routing.lead: Live view of Nepal Telecom (AS23752) as seen by RIPE RIS route collectors, with links into Hurricane Electric, Cloudflare Radar, and NTC’s own looking glass.
routing.caveat: RIPE RIS does not see every China-side path. If CTGNet (AS23764) is missing here, that does not prove the Rasuwagadhi–Kerung session is down. If it is present, that is strong evidence the BGP session is up. Corridor fiber cuts are recorded on the Status and Corridor pages, not inferred from this panel.
routing.loading: Fetching RIPE RIS… path dumps can take up to 20 seconds.
routing.error: Live RIS data is unavailable right now. Use the Hurricane Electric and RIPEstat links below.
routing.pathChipNote: Repeated AS23752 hops are prepending (NTC engineering), not extra networks.

reports.title: Field reports
reports.lead: Unofficial public notes filed as GitHub Issues. They are not NTC status, and they are not copied onto the corridor map until a maintainer verifies them.
reports.disclaimer: Anyone with a GitHub account can file a report. Treat these as tips, not official outage data. Do not post personal phone numbers or photos of people without consent.

about.title: About this board
about.lead: Independent public information for ground reports, rain, and the northern fiber board. Not a warning from NDRRMA or the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, and not a telecom operator.
about.whatBody: A comparison of weather forecasts with Department rain gauges and river gauges. Corridor and site status from named public sources. Live BGP as observed by RIPE RIS. A river page for Cyclone Arnab with cited flood clocks, open weather models, and an hourly cloud field. A crop page for cited glacial-lake counts, crop losses named in news, and a box that opens a free satellite view or a commercial imagery page. The public name is Ground check. The GitHub repository and the /NetGalchiRasuwagadi address stay as they are.
about.whatNotBody: We do not speak for NDRRMA, the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, Nepal Telecom, Ncell, NTA, China Telecom, or Starlink. This check page does not publish casualty or deployment counts. We do not score one weather model against another, or a hill gauge against a Terai model cell. We do not turn a rain gauge into a crop loss, or draw official farm plots. A box on the crop map is the viewer’s own outline. We do not take payment for satellite images. We do not mark the Galchhi–Rasuwagadhi fiber up from BGP. We do not publish how to run unlicensed satellite terminals. Starlink remains unlicensed in Nepal as of June 2026.
about.methodBody: Human-edited JSON and Markdown in git. Every status chip has an as-of time and a source. The forecast comparison is src/data/tally.json. A verdict waits until the place and the clock match a cited measurement. Crop reports and lake pins are src/data/agri.json. A hail story whose dates did not agree was left off. Routing is fetched in your browser from RIPEstat (sourceapp=netgalchi-rasuwagadhi). HE.net has no public JSON API, so we link to it rather than scrape it.
about.updateBody: Edit src/data/*.json or add a paired English/Nepali bulletin, then open a pull request. Verified field reports can be copied into sites.json by a maintainer — they are never merged automatically.
